## Concept

### Pitch

The tasks waiting their turn while their lane is busy, listed above the chat input, where they can be reordered, edited, or cancelled before they are sent.

### Shape

#### Description

The queue holds the tasks sent while their lane is busy, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, in the order they were sent unless they have been moved since. It is one list holding both lanes' queues: the code lane's and the spec lane's prompts together, in one order. Each lane sends its own prompts one at a time, first to last in that order, whenever it is free, whatever the other lane's prompts are doing, so a Spec prompt behind a Code prompt in the list is sent as soon as the spec lane is free, without waiting for the Code prompt. A Freeform prompt, which needs both lanes free, holds back the spec lane's prompts queued after it until it has been sent, so it isn't passed over for ever.

#### Lanes

Each queued prompt's row shows which lane it waits for: a small label just before its text reading its mode, "Code", "Spec", or "Freeform", tinted that mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it. A prompt sent from the Chain tab waits in the spec lane, as its first step writes the spec, and reads "Chain" in the Chain colour; a chain's later step waiting for its lane reads what it is, "Code" or "Spec follow-up", in that step's mode colour.

#### Placement

The queue sits along the bottom of the view, below the output and directly above the chat input, with a border along its top. It is not part of the header. A row saying how many prompts are queued, with a chevron, expands to list each queued prompt in order, a line or two of each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button.
Editing a queued prompt from the chat input's <Up>, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, expands the list while the queue holds more than one prompt, scrolled so the prompt being edited is in view, following it as <Up> and <Down> move the edit along the queue. Once the edit is saved or cancelled, a list it expanded collapses again; one already expanded stays as it was. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.

#### Cancel

A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer in the queue.

#### New Conversation

Each queued prompt in the list has a small toggle switch, a slider, first of its controls, switched on while the prompt will start a new conversation rather than carry on the tasks', as its hidden anchor records, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says. Clicking it switches between the two, saving the prompt again with the project. Its tooltip says which the prompt does, and that clicking does the other instead. The choice stays with the prompt wherever it is moved in the queue.
Prompts that will share a context are joined by a subtle connector line drawn between their switches: a vertical line 1 pixel wide in the theme's line colour, centred on the switches, running from the bottom of one prompt's switch to the top of the next one's, across the gap between their rows. A prompt that carries on is joined to the one above it; one that starts a new conversation is not, so each run of joined switches is one context. The first prompt in the queue is never joined to anything above it. Nothing else marks the grouping: there is no gutter, dot, or line at the row's left edge. The line follows the prompts as they are moved or switched, and is never under a switch, only between them. Each switch sits centred up and down in its row, however tall the row's text or attached images make it, and the line runs unbroken from one switch to the next across both rows' padding, with no gap where one row ends and the next begins.
The toggle can only make a prompt start a new conversation; it can't bring back one that was left. Once New conversation has been pressed for the tasks, the next task to run starts a new conversation whichever prompt it is, even when the prompt it marked has been moved further down or switched back to carrying on.

#### Reorder

Queued prompts are reordered by dragging them, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says: each row starts with a grip, and the prompt dragged follows the pointer as a line of its text. Dropped in a gap, it moves there, and the order is saved with the project, so the queue comes back in its new order when the project is opened again. A prompt still being saved, as its spinner shows, can't be dragged, and no gap past a prompt still being saved shows the indicator. A prompt being edited can still be moved, and the chat input's "Editing queued prompt N" follows it to its new place. A move that can't be saved leaves the queue as it was, and a notification titled "Could not move the prompt" says why.

#### Editing

Each queued prompt in the list also has a button with a pencil icon, after its move buttons and before its cancel button, whose tooltip says it edits the prompt. Clicking it edits the prompt in the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), as it says, and its row is highlighted while it is being edited. While it is, it is held where it is: it is never sent, and its lane, waiting on it, waits, even with auto-send on; the other lane carries on. Saving the edit puts the new text, in the mode and with the attachments it was saved with, in its place in the queue, saved with the project in place of what it held, then lets the queue go on as before. An edit that can't be saved leaves the prompt as it was, and a notification titled "Could not save the queued prompt" says why. Cancelling the edit, or cancelling the prompt from the list meanwhile, leaves the queue as it was, less that prompt when it was cancelled.

#### Queueing On Purpose

A prompt queued on purpose from the chat input's send menu, while its lane is free, waits at the end of the queue rather than being sent at once: it goes when "Send next" is clicked, or when the next task is in its lane is over and auto-send is on.

#### Auto Send

A "Send next automatically" switch picks between sending each lane's next queued prompt as soon as that lane is free, and waiting. It starts switched on, and holds for both lanes. Switching it on sends the next queued prompt of each free lane straight away. Whenever a queued prompt's lane is free, a "Send next" button sends the first such prompt in the list; with both lanes free and prompts of each queued, clicking it again sends the other lane's.

#### Persistence

Queued prompts are saved with the project's data as they are queued, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says. The queue is restored the first time the project is opened in a launch; a restored queue waits for "Send next" rather than sending on its own. A queued prompt's file is removed when it is cancelled, or when it is sent, at which point it is saved to the prompt history like any other prompt.

## Concept

### Pitch

How anything that can be reordered by dragging shows where it will end up, as macOS lists and tab bars do: with a line in the gap between two items, never a highlighted item that leaves the drop ambiguous. Every list, tab bar, or row of items that is reordered by drag and drop behaves this way.

### Shape

#### Description

While an item is dragged over the items it can be reordered among, what it would be dropped into is always a gap between two items, or before the first or after the last, never an item itself. That gap is shown by an insertion indicator, and nothing else marks the drop: no item is highlighted, tinted, or outlined as a target.

#### Indicator

The indicator is a line 2 pixels thick in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope)'s accent, with rounded ends and a small open circle, 6 pixels across and in the same colour, at its leading end. It lies across the gap, centred on the gap, horizontal between the rows of a list, running the list's width less its padding, and vertical between the tabs of a tab bar or the items of a row, running their height. It is drawn over the items, taking no room of its own, so nothing moves to make space while the drag is under way, and it never takes the mouse.

#### Choosing The Gap

Which gap is shown follows the pointer: over the first half of an item, the gap before it; over the second half, the gap after it, halves taken along the direction the items run. Past the last item, the gap after it; before the first, the gap before it. The two gaps either side of the dragged item itself are where it already is, so neither shows an indicator, and dropping there changes nothing. A gap an item may not be dropped into, as its user says, shows no indicator either, and nothing is marked while the pointer is over it.
The indicator moves from gap to gap at once as the pointer crosses the middle of an item, with no animation, so it is always exactly where a drop would land.

#### Dragging

The item dragged follows the pointer as a small floating copy, the item's own label on a raised surface with a soft shadow, as its user says. The item stays where it was in the list, dimmed to half its opacity, until it is dropped.

#### Dropping

Released over a gap that shows the indicator, the item moves into that gap, the items between shifting over by one. Released anywhere else, outside the items, over a gap it may not go into, or back where it started, nothing changes. Either way the indicator and the dimming go at once.

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/project-data import ProjectDataScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModesScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope
from /ui/behaviours/drag-reorder import DragReorderBehaviour
from /ui/components/scrollbar import ScrollbarScope

export ui-component QueueListScope:
    concept: {QueueListConcept}

concept QueueListConcept:
    pitch:
        The tasks waiting their turn while their lane is busy, listed above the
        chat input, where they can be reordered, edited, or cancelled before
        they are sent.

    shape: {QueueListShape}

shape QueueListShape:
    description:
        The queue holds the tasks sent while their lane is busy, as the
        @{PromptSendingScope} says, in the order they were sent unless they
        have been moved since. It is one list holding both lanes' queues: the
        code lane's and the spec lane's prompts together, in one order. Each
        lane sends its own prompts one at a time, first to last in that order,
        whenever it is free, whatever the other lane's prompts are doing, so a
        Spec prompt behind a Code prompt in the list is sent as soon as the
        spec lane is free, without waiting for the Code prompt. A Freeform
        prompt, which needs both lanes free, holds back the spec lane's
        prompts queued after it until it has been sent, so it isn't passed
        over for ever.

    lanes:
        Each queued prompt's row shows which lane it waits for: a small label
        just before its text reading its mode, "Code", "Spec", or "Freeform",
        tinted that mode's colour, as the @{PromptModesScope} colours it. A
        prompt sent from the Chain tab waits in the spec lane, as its first
        step writes the spec, and reads "Chain" in the Chain colour; a chain's
        later step waiting for its lane reads what it is, "Code" or "Spec
        follow-up", in that step's mode colour.

    placement:
        The queue sits along the bottom of the view, below the output and
        directly above the chat input, with a border along its top. It is not
        part of the header. A row saying how many prompts are queued, with a
        chevron, expands to list each queued prompt in order, a line or two of
        each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered,
        with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its
        row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a @{ScrollbarScope}.
        Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the
        prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last
        closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next"
        button.

        Editing a queued prompt from the chat input's <Up>, as the
        @{ChatInputScope} says, expands the list while the queue holds more
        than one prompt, scrolled so the prompt being edited is in view,
        following it as <Up> and <Down> move the edit along the queue. Once
        the edit is saved or cancelled, a list it expanded collapses again;
        one already expanded stays as it was.
        The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.

    cancel:
        A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which
        removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer
        in the queue.

    newConversation:
        Each queued prompt in the list has a small toggle switch, a slider,
        first of its controls, switched on while the prompt will start a new
        conversation rather than carry on the tasks', as its hidden anchor
        records, as the @{ChatInputScope} says. Clicking it switches between
        the two, saving the prompt again with the project. Its tooltip says
        which the prompt does, and that clicking does the other instead. The
        choice stays with the prompt wherever it is moved in the queue.

        Prompts that will share a context are joined by a subtle connector
        line drawn between their switches: a vertical line 1 pixel wide in
        the theme's line colour, centred on the switches, running from the
        bottom of one prompt's switch to the top of the next one's, across
        the gap between their rows. A prompt that carries on is joined to the
        one above it; one that starts a new conversation is not, so each run
        of joined switches is one context. The first prompt in the queue is
        never joined to anything above it. Nothing else marks the grouping:
        there is no gutter, dot, or line at the row's left edge. The line
        follows the prompts as they are moved or switched, and is never under
        a switch, only between them. Each switch sits centred up and down in its
        row, however tall the row's text or attached images make it, and the
        line runs unbroken from one switch to the next across both rows'
        padding, with no gap where one row ends and the next begins.

        The toggle can only make a prompt start a new conversation; it can't
        bring back one that was left. Once New conversation has been pressed
        for the tasks, the next task to run starts a new conversation
        whichever prompt it is, even when the prompt it marked has been moved
        further down or switched back to carrying on.

    reorder:
        Queued prompts are reordered by dragging them, as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says: each row starts with a grip, and the
        prompt dragged follows the pointer as a line of its text. Dropped in a
        gap, it moves there, and the order is saved with the project, so the
        queue comes back in its new order when the project is opened again. A
        prompt still being saved, as its spinner shows, can't be dragged, and
        no gap past a prompt still being saved shows the indicator. A prompt being edited can still be moved,
        and the chat input's "Editing queued prompt N" follows it to its new
        place. A move that can't be saved leaves the queue as it was, and a
        notification titled "Could not move the prompt" says why.

    editing:
        Each queued prompt in the list also has a button with a pencil icon,
        after its move buttons and before its cancel button, whose tooltip
        says it edits the prompt. Clicking it edits the prompt in the
        @{ChatInputScope}, as it says, and its row is highlighted while it is
        being edited. While it is, it is held where it is: it is never sent,
        and its lane, waiting on it, waits, even with auto-send on; the other
        lane carries on. Saving the
        edit puts the new text, in the mode and with the attachments it was
        saved with, in its place in the queue, saved with the project in
        place of what it held, then lets the queue go on as before. An edit
        that can't be saved leaves the prompt as it was, and a notification
        titled "Could not save the queued prompt" says why. Cancelling the
        edit, or cancelling the prompt from the list meanwhile, leaves the
        queue as it was, less that prompt when it was cancelled.

    queueingOnPurpose:
        A prompt queued on purpose from the chat input's send menu, while its
        lane is free, waits at the end of the queue rather than being sent
        at once: it goes when "Send next" is clicked, or when the next task is
        in its lane is over and auto-send is on.

    autoSend:
        A "Send next automatically" switch picks between sending each lane's
        next queued prompt as soon as that lane is free, and waiting. It starts
        switched on, and holds for both lanes. Switching it on sends the next
        queued prompt of each free lane straight away. Whenever a queued
        prompt's lane is free, a "Send next" button sends the first such
        prompt in the list; with both lanes free and prompts of each queued,
        clicking it again sends the other lane's.

    persistence:
        Queued prompts are saved with the project's data as they are queued,
        as the @{ProjectDataScope} says. The queue is restored the first time
        the project is opened in a launch; a restored queue waits for "Send
        next" rather than sending on its own. A queued prompt's file is
        removed when it is cancelled, or when it is sent, at which point it is
        saved to the prompt history like any other prompt.

use /lib
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export scope DragReorderBehaviour:
    concept: {DragReorderBehaviourConcept}

concept DragReorderBehaviourConcept:
    pitch:
        How anything that can be reordered by dragging shows where it will
        end up, as macOS lists and tab bars do: with a line in the gap between
        two items, never a highlighted item that leaves the drop ambiguous.
        Every list, tab bar, or row of items that is reordered by drag and
        drop behaves this way.

    shape: {DragReorderBehaviourShape}

shape DragReorderBehaviourShape:
    description:
        While an item is dragged over the items it can be reordered among,
        what it would be dropped into is always a gap between two items, or
        before the first or after the last, never an item itself. That gap is
        shown by an insertion indicator, and nothing else marks the drop: no
        item is highlighted, tinted, or outlined as a target.

    indicator:
        The indicator is a line 2 pixels thick in the @{ThemeScope}'s accent,
        with rounded ends and a small open circle, 6 pixels across and in the
        same colour, at its leading end. It lies across the gap, centred on
        the gap, horizontal between the rows of a list, running the list's
        width less its padding, and vertical between the tabs of a tab bar or
        the items of a row, running their height. It is drawn over the items,
        taking no room of its own, so nothing moves to make space while the
        drag is under way, and it never takes the mouse.

    choosingTheGap:
        Which gap is shown follows the pointer: over the first half of an
        item, the gap before it; over the second half, the gap after it,
        halves taken along the direction the items run. Past the last item,
        the gap after it; before the first, the gap before it. The two gaps
        either side of the dragged item itself are where it already is, so
        neither shows an indicator, and dropping there changes nothing. A gap
        an item may not be dropped into, as its user says, shows no indicator
        either, and nothing is marked while the pointer is over it.

        The indicator moves from gap to gap at once as the pointer crosses the
        middle of an item, with no animation, so it is always exactly where a
        drop would land.

    dragging:
        The item dragged follows the pointer as a small floating copy, the
        item's own label on a raised surface with a soft shadow, as its user
        says. The item stays where it was in the list, dimmed to half its
        opacity, until it is dropped.

    dropping:
        Released over a gap that shows the indicator, the item moves into that
        gap, the items between shifting over by one. Released anywhere else,
        outside the items, over a gap it may not go into, or back where it
        started, nothing changes. Either way the indicator and the dimming go
        at once.

content.text:
Queued prompts now show as one line each, clicking one opens it in the editor, and dragging scrolls the list. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 81 files.

## What changed in the spec

**Queue rows** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#placement`)
- **One line per row:** every row is 28px tall and shows only the prompt's first non-blank line. It's cut off with an ellipsis and never wraps.
- **Images:** attached images show as a small muted icon with a count, such as "2", never the images themselves.
- **Tooltip:** shows the prompt's first few lines.
- **Click to edit:** clicking the text, or anywhere in the row except its grip, switch and buttons, opens the whole prompt in the chat input with its tab selected. This does what the pencil button already does.
- **Drag from the grip:** a press on the grip that turns into a drag reorders the row instead of opening it.

**Drag reordering** (`.claude/reference/ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#scrolling-while-dragging`)

This is a new section, and it applies to every drag-to-reorder list, not just the queue.
- **Auto-scroll near the edges:** while you drag, holding the pointer within 32px of a scrolling list's edge, or past it, scrolls the list that way.
  - It starts slow and speeds up the closer or further past you go, up to about a row every 50ms.
